expected_routine_digests.description: Reviewed routine definition digests keyed by routine slug; {} when the candidate declares no call actions. A 409 with conflict:"routines" names the ones that moved.

reviewed_code.description: Attests that the whole change was reviewed. Refused with 403 when a panel the caller may not read differs between the live definition and the candidate — including on a rollback, which replaces the live definition too. That is not a state conflict and carries no conflict kind: refetching cannot change it, and no flag waives it. Read baseline.withheld_changed on the review snapshot before publishing.

definition.description: The live Page document, read from the same stored row and in the same request as definition_digest, so the comparison a reviewer reads and the value the publication is fenced on describe one instant. Panels this caller may not read are removed — panel visibility is its owning crew's, and an edit grant is not a read grant — and the same panels are removed from candidate.definition, so a withheld panel is absent from the comparison instead of appearing as one side adding it. Null only when the stored document cannot be read as a Page document; there is then no basis for a comparison. Full project and revision reads require visibility of every declared panel; source-review endpoints omit the definition.

definition_diverged.description: The live Page definition and the definition the live publication shipped with have drifted apart — somebody changed panels outside the application flow. Advisory: show it, do not refuse on it. The comparison on this snapshot is derived from the CURRENT live definition and the candidate, so it is complete regardless, and publishing the candidate is what ends the divergence. Not the definition_moved blocker, which is reserved for the publish fence tripping — a base that moved between the render and the click, where refreshing is the cure. False when there is no live publication to have diverged from, and true in the withdrawn state too, where published is false and nothing is running.

excluded_panels.description: How many panels were withheld from this comparison, counting a panel withheld from both documents once, so the screen can say its comparison is partial. Zero when neither document rendered. definition_digest is unaffected: it is always the digest of the full stored document.

source_unavailable_reason.description: A sentence shown where the comparison would have been. Unavailable is never the same as unchanged.

withheld_changed.description: At least one withheld panel differs between the live definition and the candidate: added, removed, modified, or re-pointed between a crew this caller may see and one they may not. False means the comparison on screen covers everything that moves. True adds the withheld_change blocker and the publication is refused with 403 on every path, including rollback: reviewed_code=true attests that the whole change was reviewed, and a publisher who cannot read part of it cannot make that claim. Ownership is permission to perform the operation and is not evidence about what was read; a workspace administrator sees every panel, so this is never true for one. No flag waives it. Nothing about what changed is disclosed.

code.description: definition_moved is reserved for the publish fence tripping; a standing divergence between the live definition and the published one is baseline.definition_diverged and is advisory.

icon.description: The page's icon: a crew icon name (the crew icon picker's set, lib/crew-icons.ts), or empty for the default page glyph. Refused by name outside the set.

owner.description: `user/<id>` or `crew/<slug>` — exactly one of the two (§7.1 rule 1).

pages_version.description: Changes with every change to the page's folder membership. A move or removal carries it as its fence and is refused with 409 when it is stale.

panels.description: Every panel on the page, in spec order. A panel owned by a crew the caller does not belong to arrives as the sealed placeholder — decided server-side, before serialisation, never hidden client-side (§7.1 rule 5, §11b.14).

data.description: The last payload, exactly as the producer sent it. Absent when nothing has ever been pushed.

icon.description: Optional. The panel's glyph, from a CLOSED set (internal/pages/icons.go) — a name the client has no glyph for would render a blank header, which is a quieter failure than an unknown schema. Absent means the icon the panel's schema implies. There is no per-icon colour: colour on a panel means state.

id.description: The author-chosen panel id. It is the address a producer pushes to, so it is stable across edits.

owner.description: `crew/<slug>`. This is the ACL, not a label: a viewer outside the crew never receives the panel (§7.1 rule 2).

producer.description: `<kind>/<ref>`, kind ∈ {routine, script, agent, webhook}. Only the declared producer may write the panel's payload (§7.1 rule 4).
The panel's declared producer, `<kind>/<ref>`. Server-attached (§4 rule 5): a producer never claims it.

run_id.description: The pipeline run that produced the payload. A script or webhook producer has no run, and carries the push's own server-side reference (`push:<panel>:<seq>`) instead.

reason.description: Why a failed panel failed. Internal vocabulary — never rendered on a public page (§7.3.2b).

schema.description: The set is CLOSED — a new panel kind is a server release. Five are always producible; embed.v1 is producible only where the operator has vetted an allow-list (CREWSHIP_PAGES_EMBED_SOURCES), so on an instance with none a page spec cannot declare one.

sla_seconds.description: Required and greater than zero: a panel without an SLA does not validate, and there is no default that means "never mind" (§4 rule 1).

span.description: 1–12 columns of the grid. Absent means 12.

state.description: Computed SERVER-side on every read (§4 rule 2, §11b.8). fresh and stale are functions of the clock and are never stored.

tab.description: Optional. The tab this panel renders under (internal/pages/tabs.go). Bar order is FIRST APPEARANCE in the panel list, and a panel with no tab lands on the first tab; a page where no panel declares one has no bar. Each tab carries the worst state of its own panels, and the page's freshness summary is computed over ALL tabs — a hidden tab must never be a place a panel can go stale quietly (§4).

panel.description: A token is bound to exactly ONE panel, so a leaked token can write that panel and nothing else.
